expected_behavior: regression for the ownership-count bug where uniq -c's own leading 'COUNT TOKEN' output was re-split on bare whitespace: a multi-word backticked token (`mvn clean install`) smeared across awk fields ($2 became only 'mvn'), so its true owner count of 1 was never matched and the token fell through to the shared bucket

skills/one's description names `mvn clean install` in a 'Use for ...' trigger sentence and no other skill claims that token; skills/two exists solely to give the ownership table a second skill to compare against, anchored on the unrelated single-word token `prettier`
`validate-skills.sh --anchors` on this fixture must report {"one": ["mvn clean install"], "two": ["prettier"]} — the multi-word token is correctly attributed to its sole owner

because ownership is now counted correctly, one's unique multi-word token must NOT trigger NO-UNIQUE-ANCHOR (it is not structurally un-anchorable) or ANCHOR-COLLISION (its trigger sentence's token is not shared); the token is also already named in the trigger sentence, so ANCHOR-NOT-STATED must not fire either
